title: From Approximation to Emergence: A Theory of Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning has outgrown any single mathematical explanation. From Approximation to Emergence develops a unified, proof-oriented account of modern deep learning theory, tracing a path from the classical foundations of approximation, optimization, and generalization to the contemporary mechanisms of overparameterization, robustness, generative modeling, transformers, in-context learning, scaling laws, interpretability, alignment, and emergence. Rather than presenting isolated results, the book organizes a broad literature into a coherent research narrative: each theory is examined through the object it controls, the assumptions that make it valid, and the phenomena it leaves unexplained. Written for researchers, graduate students, and mathematically trained practitioners, this monograph offers a rigorous map of deep learning theory as it stands today: powerful, incomplete, and increasingly centered on the question of how learned mechanisms arise from scale, data, architecture, and training.

title: Development of a post quantum cryptography algorithm
abstract: Η ανάδυση μεγάλης κλίμακας κβαντικών υπολογιστών αποτελεί θεμελιώδη απειλή για την ασφάλεια των κλασικών κρυπτογραφικών σχημάτων δημοσίου κλειδιού, συμπεριλαμβανομένων του RSA και της κρυπτογραφίας ελλειπτικών καμπυλών (ECC). Ο αλγόριθμος Shor [6], εκτελούμενος σε επαρκώς ισχυρό κβαντικό υπολογιστή, επιλύει το πρόβλημα παραγοντοποίησης ακεραίων και το πρόβλημα του διακριτού λογαρίθμου σε πολυωνυμικό χρόνο, καθιστώντας τα κρυπτοσυστήματα RSA και ECC ανασφαλή. Ως απόκριση, αναπτύχθηκε η Μετα-Κβαντική Κρυπτογραφία (Post-Quantum Cryptography, PQC), στην οποία εντάσσεται το κρυπτοσύστημα NTRU — ένα από τα παλαιότερα και πλέον αναλυμένα κρυπτοσυστήματα βασισμένα σε πλέγματα. Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία παρουσιάζει μια πλήρη υλοποίηση του κρυπτοσυστήματος NTRU-HPS (N=509, p=3, q=2048, επίπεδο ασφάλειας ≈128 bit) σε FPGA, αναπτυγμένη με χρήση του Vivado / Vitis High-Level Synthesis (HLS) 2024.2 της AMD Xilinx. Η υλοποίηση σε C/C++ καλύπτει τις τρεις κεντρικές λειτουργίες του κρυπτοσυστήματος: παραγωγή κλειδιών (keygen), κρυπτογράφηση (encryption) και αποκρυπτογράφηση (decryption). Ο κώδικας βελτιστοποιείται μέσω pragma οδηγιών HLS, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των HLS PIPELINE (II=1), HLS ARRAY_PARTITION CYCLIC και HLS DATAFLOW. Η συσκευή-στόχος είναι το FPGA Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ ZCU104 (XCZU7EV-FFVC1156-2-E). Κατά τη διαδικασία ανάπτυξης εντοπίστηκαν και διορθώθηκαν δύο κρίσιμα μαθηματικά σφάλματα: (α) η κατασκευή του ιδιωτικού κλειδιού f, η οποία πρέπει να ακολουθεί τη μορφή f = 1 + p·F (αντί απλού τριαδικού πολυωνύμου) για να εξασφαλίζεται η αντιστρεψιμότητά του στον δακτύλιο R_p, και (β) ο αλγόριθμος αντιστροφής πολυωνύμων, ο οποίος απαιτεί πλήρη πολυωνυμική διαίρεση (long division with remainder) σε κάθε βήμα του Εκτεταμένου Αλγόριθμου Ευκλείδη (EEA) για ορθά αποτελέσματα σε GF(p)[x]/(x^N - 1). Η ορθότητα της υλοποίησης επαληθεύεται μέσω πλήρους κύκλου keygen → encrypt → decrypt (C-simulation), ο οποίος επιστρέφει PASS για τυχαία δεδομένα ελέγχου. Τα αποτελέσματα σύνθεσης αξιολογούνται ως προς κατανάλωση πόρων FPGA (LUTs, FFs, DSPs, BRAM), μέγιστη συχνότητα λειτουργίας και καθυστέρηση (latency), και συγκρίνονται με σχετικές προηγούμενες εργασίες της βιβλιογραφίας. Τα αποτελέσματα αποδεικνύουν ότι το Vitis HLS 2024.2 αποτελεί αποτελεσματική μεθοδολογία για πρωτοτυποποίηση κρυπτογραφικού υλικού PQC, επιτυγχάνοντας σημαντική επιτάχυνση σε σχέση με το λογισμικό αναφοράς, με μικρότερο κόστος ανάπτυξης σε σχέση με χειροκίνητο RTL σχεδιασμό.

title: Development of a chess problem composition program
abstract: Αντικείμενο της παρούσας Διπλωματικής εργασίας είναι η ανάπτυξη ενόςπρογράμματος σκακιστικών προβλημάτων, ικανό να συνθέτει προβλήματα ματ σε πεπερασμένο αριθμό κινήσεων και συγκεκριμένο θέμα. Αρχικά πραγματοποιείται μια ιστορική αναδρομή στο παιχνίδι μέχρι τις απαρχές του καλλιτεχνικού σκακιστικού χώρου.Αναλύονται τα χαρακτηριστικά και οι αρχές που διέπουν το καλλιτεχνικό σκάκι, και παρουσιάζονται οι κατηγορίες και τα θέματα που πρόκειται να αναπτυχθούν.Η ανάπτυξη του προγράμματος πραγματοποιήθηκε σε δύο στάδια. Στο πρώτοδημιουργήθηκε ένα σύστημα το οποίο κατασκευάζει σκακιστικά προβλήματα ματ σε έναν πεπερασμένο αριθμό Ν κινήσεων, βασιζόμενο στη δομή ενός αλγορίθμου generate and test. Στο δεύτερο και πιο σύνθετο στάδιο, αναπτύχθηκε ένα σύστημα ικανό να κατασκευάζει σκακιστικά προβλήματα με σύνθετα καλλιτεχνικά θέματα, πιο συγκεκριμένα: Novotny, Albino, Allumwandlung. Για τον σκοπό αυτό επιστρατεύτηκαν δύο διαφορετικές αλγοριθμικές προσεγγίσεις: Γενετικοί Αλγόριθμοι και Βελτιστοποίηση Αποικίας Μυρμηγκιών.Για την υλοποίηση των παραπάνω προγραμμάτων έγινε χρήση της γλώσσαςπρογραμματισμού Python, καθώς και εξειδικευμένων βιβλιοθηκών όπως η «python-chess» κ.α. Ως μονάδα επικύρωσης και αξιολόγησης των συνθέσεων χρησιμοποιήθηκε η σκακιστική μηχανή «Stockfish» και η πλατφόρμα «lichess.org».Το κείμενο περιλαμβάνει μία αναλυτική περιγραφή των αλγορίθμων, τουσχεδιασμού τους, καθώς και των συναρτήσεων που συνέθεσαν τα αντίστοιχαπρογράμματα. Τέλος παρουσιάζονται τα σημαντικότερα αποτελέσματα από τους πειραματισμούς, καθώς και μια σύγκριση μεταξύ των δύο αλγορίθμων.Τα αποτελέσματα και οι πειραματισμοί, αναδεικνύουν τη συνεισφορά της εργασίας στην αξιοποίηση των εξελικτικών αλγορίθμων ως εργαλείου υπολογιστικήςδημιουργικότητας. Συνολικά το σύστημα μπορεί να αποτελέσει πηγή έμπνευσης ως ψηφιακός συνεργάτης σε ένα σκακιστικό συνθέτη, καθώς και ανοίγει δρόμους για βελτιώσεις.Ο κώδικας της εργασίας είναι διαθέσιμος στο Github μέσω του παρακάτω συνδέσμου: https://github.com/ektoraslamb-beep/Development-of-a-chess-problem-composition program

title: Integrating self-supervised representations with semi-supervised self-organising maps for geological facies delineation in the Mundi Mundi region, Australia
abstract: Regional exploration geophysical surveys typically produce multi-parameter datasets covering large areas. Such datasets yield valuable insights into the subsurface, but their complexity may require advanced analytical methods to interpret them. The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence provides powerful tools to make this task easier. Self-organising maps (SOMs) are a form of unsupervised artificial neural network used for clustering large multi-variate datasets. SOMs can detect underlying patterns and trends within multi-parameter geophysical datasets, producing petrophysical cluster maps that can be subsequently interpreted to infer lithological boundaries and geological structures. In this study, we integrated self-supervised representation learning with a semi-supervised SOM to delineate geological facies from multi-variate geophysical data in the Mundi Mundi region of the Curnamona Province, Australia. A self-supervised neural network was first trained on five independent geophysical datasets (with no labels) to learn an informative 32-dimensional embedding that captures combined spatial and multi-modal structure in the data. We then enhanced the SOM through a hybrid training approach, utilising existing mapped geological units only as weak supervision to anchor the model and name the resulting clusters, while still allowing the data to primarily drive the organisation. Unlike conventional hard clustering, our method used fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering on the SOM’s best-matching units, enabling the delineation of gradational geological boundaries and explicit mapping of zones of uncertainty. A sparse use of geological labels guided the clustering without imposing a rigid classification, and class-aware learning vector quantisation fine-tuned the SOM prototypes to better align with known classes. The availability of an interpreted basement geological map enabled assessment of agreement between SOM-derived facies and the existing geological interpretation. The SOM successfully identified and mapped distinctive geophysical signatures corresponding to various geological units delineated in the existing regional geological map, but significantly also highlighted inconsistencies between the clustered petrophysical properties and those expected for some units within the previously interpreted geology. The results demonstrate that SOMs, when combined with self-supervised feature learning, fuzzy clustering, and minimal geological supervision, can uncover latent patterns in multi-modal geophysical datasets and offer a robust tool for regional-scale subsurface lithological mapping to guide exploration targeting.

title: AI-Powered English Teaching Model Integrating Multimodal Corpora and Deep Learning in the Context of Digitalization
abstract: Traditional English teaching often lacks integration between intelligent analysis and multimodal teaching principles in digital learning environments. This study proposes an end to-end AI-powered English teaching model that combines multimodal corpora with deep learning technologies. A synchronized multimodal teaching corpus was developed to integrate audio, visual, textual, and behavioral data. The model uses a hierarchical deep learning architecture with dedicated encoders and a cross-modal attention fusion mechanism to generate unified representations. A multi-task collaborative learning framework performs four key diagnostic functions simultaneously: pronunciation assessment, grammatical error detection, learning engagement classification, and knowledge tracking. Based on these diagnostic outcomes, a reinforcement learning agent using the proximal policy optimization algorithm provides personalized learning recommendations. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves superior performance across multiple tasks and significantly improves learning outcomes, including a 26.2% reduction in learning time for the experimental group. The study offers an effective approach for developing adaptive, precise, and intelligent digital English teaching systems.

title: SoK: Multi-Perspective-Video-Anonymization
abstract: Video data has become central in many modern systems, from public surveillance to autonomous vehicles, but its widespread use raises serious concerns about exposing people’s identities and behaviors. This survey takes a structured look at how recent research has tried to address these concerns through video anonymization. We conduct a systematic review of the literature and organize existing work into a taxonomy that separates different anonymization strategies, the visual regions they target, and the assumptions they make about the video setting. By examining these categories, we highlight how current methods approach privacy protection and where they tend to fall short. A consistent pattern across the field is that most studies are designed for single-view videos, even though many real environments involve multiple synchronized cameras. Only a handful of works consider this multi-perspective setting, revealing a clear disconnect between research and real-world needs. We also review the datasets and evaluation metrics commonly used in anonymization studies and show that they rarely capture multi-view complexity, underscoring the need for more representative benchmarks. Finally, we discuss the utility goals that anonymization methods aim to preserve and outline key gaps that future work must address to support practical, multi-camera video applications.

title: A Benchmark Comparison of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Flash on Problem Solving Performance in Text-Based Classical Mechanics Word Problems: An Evaluation of Selected End-Chapter Problems From Young & Freedman's 15th Edition University Physics Textbook
abstract: Abstract: The study measures the text-based problem solving accuracy of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Flash in mechanics. The research aims to solve three questions: (1) both model’s overall accuracy across the full sample, (2) accuracy by chapter, (3) and the magnitude and statistical genuineness of accuracy gap between models. The models were evaluated using a set of 416 odd-numbered end chapter problems under the 14-chapter mechanics unit of 15th Edition University Physics Textbook by Young & Freedman. Each problem, along with a system prompt and temperature parameter set to 0, were sent as a single API call. The correctness of both model’s answers were evaluated manually against the available answer key. Wilson’s score interval (95% CI) was applied as another statistical layer to assess the genuine performance gap between models by accounting the small and uneven problem spread by chapter. Overall, DeepSeek V4 Pro achieved 95.43% accuracy while DeepSeek V4 Flash achieved 94.71% accuracy. Both models scored identically in 10 out of 14 chapters. The 4 non-identical scoring chapters attained single-digit percentage gaps ranging from 3.33 to 5.88%. Among those 4 chapters, Pro outperformed Flash in 3 chapters, while Flash only outscored the other beating in 1 chapter. Overlap factors between models for both overall each 14 chapters exceed the 0.5 mark, indicating that the observed accuracy gaps are merely descriptive and do not suggest any genuine performance gap

title: Granularity Effects in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer for XTREME-Retrieval
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the choice of intermediate task granularity (e.g., fine-grained vs. coarse-grained) impact zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-Retrieval when comparing models trained on multilingual versus English-only intermediate tasks? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.0/10.

title: ЕВОЛЮЦІЯ КОМП'ЮТЕРНИХ НАУК В УМОВАХ РОЗВИТКУ АГЕНТНОГО ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ
abstract: ЕВОЛЮЦІЯ КОМП'ЮТЕРНИХ НАУК В УМОВАХ РОЗВИТКУ АГЕНТНОГО ШТУЧНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ Анотація.У цій статті досліджується фундаментальна трансформація життєвого циклу розробки програмного забезпечення (SDLC) та академічної дисципліни комп'ютерних наук під впливом агентного штучного інтелекту.На відміну від традиційних інструментів автодоповнення коду, сучасні агентні ШІ-системи здатні автономно сприймати інформацію, міркувати, планувати та виконувати багатоетапні інженерні завдання з мінімальним втручанням людини.Розглядається перехід від розрізнених точкових рішень до інтегрованих платформ автоматизації SDLC, які об'єднують процеси від збору вимог до тестування та розгортання в єдину інтелектуальну систему.Впровадження таких архітектур забезпечує прискорення циклів розгортання на 30-50% та суттєве зниження витрат на забезпечення якості.Окрему увагу приділено докорінній еволюції ролі інженера-програміста. Основний фокус діяльності зміщується від тактичного написання коду до стратегічного архітектурного проєктування, декомпозиції завдань та оркестрування скоординованих команд автономних ШІ-агентів.Критично аналізуються нові ризики цієї зміни парадигми, зокрема феномен «vibe coding» -стрімкої генерації коду без глибокого системного розуміння, що неминуче призводить до накопичення технічного боргу та архітектурної нестабільності.Водночас наголошується на імперативі вбудовування механізмів безпеки та нормативної відповідності (наприклад, жорстким вимогам EU AI Act щодо нагляду за високоризиковими системами) безпосередньо у життєвий цикл розробки.У контексті трансформації вищої освіти, зокрема підготовки за спеціальністю F3 «Комп'ютерні науки», стаття обґрунтовує необхідність концептуального оновлення освітніх стандартів.Підкреслюється, що класичні навички алгоритмізації мають бути доповнені компетенціями інженерії систем штучного інтелекту повного циклу, практиками MLOps, забезпеченням безпеки ШІ та інтелектуальним аналізом даних.Визначено, що для збереження релевантності сучасні комп'ютерні науки мусять еволюціонувати від парадигм № 5(59) 2026

title: Study of The Ant Colony With Its Application to The Traveling Salesman Problem
abstract: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) is one of the most known nature inspired metheuristic techniques, which is basically based on the simulation of the social behaviour of ants when searching for the shortest paths between their colony and their food source. The algorithm was originally introduced in 1992 by Marco Dorigo to solve NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems which are hard to solve with traditional algorithms because of their large search space and high computational complexity. The research shows that the ant algorithm is a flexible yet powerful mathematical model that can adapt to changes occurring in dynamically changing complex systems, and that new opportunities for hybridizing with techniques of artificial intelligence/machine learning emerge for further increasing the convergence speed and the efficiency of the system. It has been used to solve the travelling salesman problem and has proved to be successful.

title: Scalable Learning of Challenging Normative Behaviours with Deep RL
abstract: The acceptance of AI agents in daily life hinges on their alignment with social, moral, and legal norms, and in recent years, attempts to build norm-sensitive AI agents --- including reinforcement learning (RL) agents --- have gained traction. However, while there are many promising approaches, they tend to be geared toward environments with modest state spaces, and adaptations to the deep RL context are lacking. In this paper we present a deep learning adaptation of normative restraining bolts (NRBs). Our contributions are twofold; first we combine NRBs with deep Q-networks (DQNs) and proximal policy optimization (PPO) to learn optimal behaviour compliant with challenging norms in a complex environment. We demonstrate our agent's ability to learn difficult normative behaviours in the game Pac-Man, which has been used in the literature to benchmark normative RL techniques. evidence.abstract: The acceptance of AI agents in daily life hinges on their alignment with social, moral, and legal norms, and in recent years, attempts to build norm-sensitive AI agents --- including reinforcement learning (RL) agents --- have gained traction. However, while there are many promising approaches, they tend to be geared toward environments with modest state spaces, and adaptations to the deep RL context are lacking. title: DeepEL: Deep Learning and Formal Description Logic Reasoning
abstract: Light-weight description logics like EL have been successfully used to represent the terminological knowledge of many application domains. Yet, identifying the characteristics of instances often requires sub-symbolic approaches. We introduce a neuro-symbolic extension of EL which allows for (neural) perception and classification of properties, accompanied by formal (symbolic) reasoning based on these perceptions. Through a prototypical implementation, based on a reduction to logic programming, we show that inferences and learning are effectively achievable.

title: Towards Automated Identification of Block Cipher Structures Using Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract This paper focuses on the classification of block ciphers based on their structure, which is a crucial step in automated cryptanalysis. For this purpose, five machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, k-Nearest Neighbour, Random Forest, and XGBoost, are applied to ciphertext data to differentiate between Substitution–Permutation Networks (SPN) and Feistel block cypher structures. A comprehensive experimental framework is developed using 16 block ciphers, including AES, DES, Blowfish, Twofish, and Camelia, etc evaluated across two encryption modes (ECB and CBC) with 5-fold cross validation under four different scenarios. To improve generalization and eliminate dataset bias, ciphertext datasets are generated using fixed key and multiple random keys and diverse plaintext sources, including text, source code, and binary data. A feature extraction pipeline based on byte-level statistics, compression characteristics, and higher-order histogram features is employed, followed by classification using five machine learning and one deep learning models. NIST SP800-22 suite tests were conducted on ciphertext dataset. Results confirmed that despite ciphertexts exhibit near-ideal entropy and pass standard randomness tests; however, small higher-order statistical deviations remain observable. Experimental results demonstrate that these weak statistical signals can be leveraged to achieve classification accuracies exceeding 90% for ciphertext, with performance increasing as ciphertext size increases. The classification accuracy is highest for ECB and decreases for CBC, consistent with increasing diffusion and inter-block dependency. Feature importance and ablation studies further reveal that statistical features provide the dominant discriminative signal. These findings highlight the presence of finite-sample statistical artifacts that can be detected using machine learning, and provide new insights into the intersection of statistical cryptanalysis and machine learning, with implications for automated cryptographic analysis.

title: A comparative evaluation of DBSCAN, optics, and HDBSCAN clustering algorithms using external validation measures
abstract: Clustering is one of the most important unsupervised learning techniques used to discover hidden patterns and structures within data. Among clustering methods, density-based algorithms have attracted significant attention due to their ability to identify clusters of arbitrary shapes and effectively handle noise. This study presents a comparative evaluation of three widely used density-based clustering algorithms: DBSCAN, OPTICS, and HDBSCAN. A simulated dataset containing multiple clusters with noise was generated to assess the performance of these algorithms under controlled conditions. The comparison was conducted using five external validation measures: Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), Normalized Mutual Information (NMI), Purity, Jaccard Index, and Fowlkes–Mallows Index (FMI). The optimal parameter values for each algorithm were determined through a systematic search process to ensure a fair comparison. The experimental results showed that OPTICS achieved the best overall performance, obtaining the highest values in NMI (0.9401), Jaccard Index (0.9567), and Fowlkes–Mallows Index (0.9780). DBSCAN produced the highest Adjusted Rand Index (0.9692) and achieved the same Purity (0.984) as OPTICS, indicating highly accurate clustering performance. In contrast, HDBSCAN demonstrated comparatively lower performance across all evaluation measures while still producing satisfactory clustering results. The findings indicate that both OPTICS and DBSCAN are highly effective density-based clustering algorithms for the simulated dataset considered in this study, with OPTICS providing the most balanced performance according to the selected external validation measures. The proposed comparison offers useful guidance for selecting appropriate density-based clustering algorithms in practical data analysis applications.

title: Interview with Akari Asai - Beyond Scaling: Frontiers of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
abstract: Akari Asai is a Research Scientist at the Allen Institute for AI (AI2) and an incoming Assistant Professor in the School of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University. She received her Ph.D. from the University of Washington. Her research advances reliable and up-to-date language systems, especially retrieval-augmented and agentic language models, and applies them to high-impact settings, including scientific discovery and information access for underrepresented languages. Akari's work has been published at top-tier NLP and ML venues and in Nature, and has been recognized with multiple paper awards, the IBM Global Fellowship, and industry grants. She is a recipient of the AAAI/ACM SIGAI Doctoral Dissertation Award, was named to MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35 and Forbes 30 Under 30 (Asia, Science), and has been featured by outlets including Forbes and MIT Technology Review.
